figures.finding: Under Niue's Minors' Contracts Act (New Zealand's 1969 Act, in force in Niue from 1970 as the consolidated laws hold it), a contract of service made by a minor, and any contract of a minor of eighteen or over, has effect as if of full age, though a court may cancel or decline to enforce it if the consideration was unconscionable or a term harsh or oppressive; any other contract of a minor under eighteen (an author's commission, a rights deal) is unenforceable against the minor unless a court finds it fair and reasonable; and any contract approved by the Court beforehand, on application by the minor, another party or a guardian, binds as if the minor were of full age. No set-aside of earnings was found.

value.binding: contract of service: binding (s. 5(1)(c)) subject to court review; other contracts under 18: unenforceable against the minor (s. 6); prior Court approval makes any contract binding (s. 9)

figures.applies: Niue (the Act consolidated in the Niue Legislation 2019, volume 2).

sources.said: (1) Subject to this section, every contract which is – (a) Entered into by a minor who has attained the age of 18 years; or (b) [Repealed] (c) A contract of service entered into by a minor; … shall have effect as if the minor were of full age.

(1) Subject to this section, every contract other than a contract to which section 5(1)(b)or (c) applies entered into by a minor who has not attained the age of 18 years shall be unenforceable against the minor but otherwise shall have effect as if the minor were of full age.

(1) Every contract entered into by a minor shall have effect as if the minor were of full age if, before the contract is entered into by the minor, it is approved under this section by the Court. (2) An application to the Court under this section may be made – (a) By the minor or any other person who will be a party to the proposed contract; or (b) By a guardian of the minor.

figures.finding: A company director in Niue must be a natural person and not under twenty-one, as the Companies Regulations' director's consent form sets out the disqualifications; an age to hold shares wasn't found.
figures.applies: Companies Act 2006 and its Regulations, as consolidated.

sources.said: A person who is not a natural person cannot be a director of a company. … A person cannot be a director of a company if he or she is any of the following: under 21 years of age;
